transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Carva Coleman.
The Trump administration is relaxing the standards that are supposed to make cars and trucks
more fuel efficient.
Biden-era rules aim to boost fuel efficiency, so the cars could get up to 50 miles to the
gallon.
The move by President Trump lowers that to 35 miles to the gallon.
NPR's Willa Rubin reports the administration and auto industry say this will save car buyers
hundreds of dollars.
In statements to NPR, automakers praise the move.
They say that the new standards are more in line with market realities, meaning EV sales
are still a minority of new car sales in the U.S., but critics say just looking at the
sticker price ignores some of the longer-term expenses that come with being a car owner.
NPR's Willa Rubin reporting, "AAA says that this morning the average cost for a gallon
of regular gas is $4.46, diesel is more than $6.40."
This morning, President Trump is poised to announce updates to the website america.gov.
AI industry leaders are expected to join him at the announcement.
Big Tech company OpenAI says it is scrapping the release of its newest AI model after it
failed to meet company internal testing standards.
NPR's John Ruich reports the decision comes after a string of reports of AI bots involved
in hacking incidents.
The company had been planning to release the model, called GPT-6.1 Astra, in the coming
days, but it's decided to scrap the release.
Sachi Jain, head of safety systems at OpenAI, said, "It didn't quite meet the bar in testing
and fell short in terms of communication with the user about the work it's done."
He told the Wall Street Journal it performed poorly on alignment, the term AI developers
use for how well a model sticks to what people want, rather than going off script.
In an emailed statement, Jain says, "When shipping new models to users, OpenAI has an
extremely high bar in terms of safety and alignment.
The company says it has other new models coming soon."
John Ruich, NPR News.
Employees at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta say that the federal
agency's work is being hampered by job cuts.
The member station WABE Jess Mador reports, "The CDC lost 30 percent or more than 3,800
employees between March of 2025 and May of this year, according to the report.
That includes hundreds of employees who were terminated, put on administrative leave or
who opted for retirement.
The Trump administration has maintained the cuts eliminated waste, fraud, and abuse in
the government."
In an emailed statement, a spokesperson for the American Federation of Government Employees
Union says the job cuts continue and amount to a dismantling of the public health infrastructure
designed to respond quickly to threats.
For NPR News, I'm Jess Mador in Atlanta.
This is NPR.
Former special counsel Jack Smith is scheduled to testify today before the Senate Judiciary
Committee.
Lawmakers are reviewing his probes of President Trump.
Some Republican lawmakers want to see Smith criminally prosecuted.
Smith says if he had the same set of facts presented to him today, he would again choose
to prosecute a president regardless of party.
Business leaders and elected officials in Jackson Hole, Wyoming are urging the U.S.
Interior Secretary to reject a proposed baseball field inside Grand Teton National Park.
From member station KHOL, Sophia Boyd Flegel reports.
Some Jackson Hole locals were shocked by a recent Washington Post report that the Trump
administration had scouted locations in Grand Teton National Park to build a baseball park
to host a major league baseball game.
NPR has not independently confirmed the report.
Rick Howe is a longtime leader of the Jackson Hole Chamber of Commerce.
I thought it was just kind of one of those conspiracy theories of jokes.
It isn't.
This isn't something we should be accepting.
Howe told commissioners that even a temporary field on already disturbed land would undermine
the purpose of the park to protect its natural resources, wildlife and serve the public.
Commissioners immediately signed onto a chamber letter asking the Interior Department to reject
the proposal and direct any other commercial events to venues that aren't protected.
For NPR News, I'm Sophia Boyd Flegel in Jackson.
Forecasters say Hurricane Polo has made landfall on Baja, California.
It is still expected to be a hurricane when it hits the Mexican mainland later today.
This message comes from Angie.
Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros to get their home projects done well
for over 30 years.
For everything from minor repairs to major remodels, find reviews, pricing and booking
at Angie.com or on the Angie app.

topics.text: Trump administration relaxes fuel efficiency standards for cars and trucks to 35 miles per gallon
President Trump poised to announce updates to website america.gov with AI industry leaders present
OpenAI scraps release of GPT-6.1 Astra model after failing internal testing and safety standards
CDC lost over 3,800 employees between March and May 2025 due to federal job cuts
Former special counsel Jack Smith scheduled to testify before Senate Judiciary Committee on Trump probes
Jackson Hole business leaders and officials urge Interior Secretary to reject proposed baseball field in Grand Teton National Park
Hurricane Polo makes landfall on Baja California, expected to reach Mexican mainland as hurricane later today
